key_insight: Change2Task turns real merged pull requests into executable coding-agent tasks by replaying them on healthy, modern repository revisions. This creates a scalable supply of realistic tasks with verified environments and ground-truth outcomes.
problem_solved: Coding agents need large amounts of executable, realistic data for training, benchmarking, and continuous evaluation, but such tasks are expensive to create and often lack reliable environments or verification. The paper addresses the shortage of high-quality tasks that combine software state, specification, tools, and automated checks.
method: Starts from repository history and selects merged pull requests as evidence of real development tasks.
Aligns historical changes with an evolved, healthy version of the same repository to reconstruct executable task environments.
Verifies tasks using reliable checks so each task includes a runnable setup, clear specification, and confirmable success criteria.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a scalable pipeline for building stronger coding-agent benchmarks and training data from authentic software evolution. It can improve evaluation realism and support continuous testing of agents on tasks that better match real-world development.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: repository history -> merged PRs -> task reconstruction -> verified executable tasks
Before/after repository state illustration highlighting historical changes mapped to modern code
Icons for code, tools, verification, and evaluation to show task components
Bar or flow chart showing scalable task generation from many pull requests
paper_title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
paper_authors: Haomin Qi, Xingliang Wang, Xuanqi Gao, Baihui Sang, Xin Zhang
